cases.question: What does the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025 say about turnover limits?

claims.text: In the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a "small business" means a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business.

In the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a "small company" means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

"Gross turnover" means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants.

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded from the taxable supplies counted, as is a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business.

<question>
What does the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025 say about turnover limits?
</question>
<gaps>

The passages do not say which of the two turnover limits applies to a particular business.

cases.rendered:
In the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a "small business" means a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

In the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a "small company" means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

"Gross turnover" means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover"]

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded from the taxable supplies counted, as is a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not include any statute called the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025. The turnover limits found are in the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Act 2025.
- The passages do not say which of the two turnover limits applies to a particular business.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover" (gazette pages A 504, A 505)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10) (gazette page A 277)

- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)

cases.question: What do sections 22 and 290 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act say about VAT returns?

claims.text: A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form, with or without a notice, and whether or not an economic activity has taken place, on or before the 21st day of the following month.
The returns must contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
If the Service grants an extension of the period for filing returns, the extension does not imply an extension of time to pay the tax.
The filing rule in subsection (1) does not apply to a small business.

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. This option does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations as defined in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025.
A business that ceases to be a small business shall file monthly VAT returns.

In deciding whether a person meets the small company threshold, the value of two kinds of taxable supplies is excluded: supply of a capital asset of the person, and supply made solely as a consequence of selling the whole or a part of the business or permanently ceasing to carry on business.
A taxable person granted the exemption in subsection (4) is exempt from sections 105 and 107 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act and section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025.
Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person shall render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe.
For the purpose of attribution, any VAT return under section 22 shall provide details of consumption of taxable supplies, irrespective of where the return is filed.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form, with or without a notice, and whether or not an economic activity has taken place, on or before the 21st day of the following month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The VAT return must contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

If the Service grants an extension of the period for filing the returns, that extension does not mean more time to pay the tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The 21st-day filing rule in subsection (1) does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A small business may, by written notice to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption given to small businesses, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. This choice does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations as defined in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A business that ceases to be a small business shall file monthly VAT returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person shall render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, in accordance with the Act, is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs and ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. cases.rendered:
A development levy of 4% is imposed on the assessable profits of all companies chargeable to tax under Chapters Two and Three of the Act, other than small companies and non-resident companies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 59]

A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

The development levy shall not be levied on assessable profits computed for the purposes of hydrocarbon tax. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 59]

Assessable profit has the same meaning under the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 for the purposes of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "assessable profit"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The levy amount needs a calculation (applying the 4% rate to the assessable profit), which is not done here.
- The passages do not say whether the company is resident, whether it is chargeable under Chapters Two and Three, or whether its assessable profit is computed for hydrocarbon tax.
- The company's total fixed assets and whether it provides professional services are not given, though they matter only if it could be a small company; the stated turnover is above the small company turnover limit.
- The passages do not say how assessable profit is worked out, so whether the stated figure is the correct base for the levy cannot be confirmed.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 59 (gazette page A 427)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "assessable profit" (gazette page A 327)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)

cases.question: I filed my company's VAT return three months late. What is the total penalty?

claims.text: A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs.
The same provision adds an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues.

Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, and subject to section 67, a sum equal to 10% of the tax payable is added to it, and the tax carries interest from the date it becomes payable until it is paid.
For naira remittances, that interest is at the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread to be determined by the Minister.
For foreign currency remittances, that interest is at the prevailing Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") or any successor rate, plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines.
The penalty and interest under section 65 are not deemed part of the tax paid for the purpose of claiming relief under the Act or any other tax law.

This rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.

A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority.
For a donation other than in cash, the value for the purpose of section 164 is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired.

VAT is paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 145]

VAT is charged on the value of all taxable supplies at the rate of 7.5%, subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 148]

The value of an imported taxable supply is the price of the taxable supply imported, plus taxes, duties and other charges levied either outside or by reason of importation into Nigeria, other than VAT imposed under the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 150]

The value of an imported taxable supply also includes costs by way of commission, parking, transport and insurance up to the port or point of entry. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 150]

The Act defines "machinery" as a mechanical device or the parts that operate together to perform a single task, including the accessories necessary to the working of a machine. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 189, definition of "machinery"]

- The passages do not say that the imported machine parts are a taxable supply, or whether they are covered by an exemption in Part IV of Chapter Eight.

- Part IV of Chapter Eight, to which the VAT charge is made subject, is only partly among the passages, so the exemptions it sets out are not shown.
- The VAT amount and the total value for the import need a calculation, which is not done here.

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. For a small company, the rate is 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A company that is not a small company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. A business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Where the effective tax rate of a company in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The question text includes a statement that small companies pay 5%. The section 56 passage as printed gives a different rate, so the 5% figure is not stated in the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)

Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.question: We bought ₦9 million of office furniture. How much capital allowance can we claim each year?

claims.text: Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is a type of qualifying capital expenditure (qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure).
Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2 of Table I, with a rate of 20%.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance at the rate specified in Table I is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business.
The allowance is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of the basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.

The proviso also says 1% of qualifying capital expenditure is recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes until the asset is disposed of. It is a notional amount and does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable.

The residue of a qualifying expenditure at any date is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before that date for the asset, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date.

An allowance is not made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
Where an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it is carried forward to subsequent period.

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the year. If there is no remainder or not enough remainder, the deduction or the part not yet made is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised.

gaps: The amount of allowance each year needs a calculation applying the Class 2 rate to the expenditure, which is not done here.
The passages do not say whether the rate applies to the original cost each year or to the residue after earlier allowances.
The passages do not say whether the office furniture falls within qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure, or whether it is used wholly and exclusively for the trade or business.
The passages do not state the business's basis period or whether it is owned and in use at the end of that period.

cases.rendered:
Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is a type of qualifying capital expenditure (qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure). [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraph 1, definition of "qualifying capital expenditure", paragraph (j)]

Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2 of Table I, with a rate of 20%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, Table I, Capital Allowance]

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance at the rate specified in Table I is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

The allowance is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of the basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

The proviso also says 1% of qualifying capital expenditure is recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes until the asset is disposed of. It is a notional amount and does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

The residue of a qualifying expenditure at any date is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before that date for the asset, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

An allowance is not made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

Where an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it is carried forward to subsequent period. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the year. If there is no remainder or not enough remainder, the deduction or the part not yet made is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

1 statement was removed because the cited provisions did not support it.

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The amount of allowance each year needs a calculation applying the Class 2 rate to the expenditure, which is not done here.
- The passages do not say whether the rate applies to the original cost each year or to the residue after earlier allowances.
- The passages do not say whether the office furniture falls within qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure, or whether it is used wholly and exclusively for the trade or business.
- The passages do not state the business's basis period or whether it is owned and in use at the end of that period.

claims.text: From the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the Companies Income Tax Act, Cap. C21, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004 is repealed.

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 has its own income tax exemption provision. It exempts from tax under chapter two the profits or gains of listed persons, such as certain friendly societies, co-operative societies, bodies engaged in educational, religious or charitable activities of a public character, and registered trade unions, where the profits or gains are not derived from a trade or business carried on by them.

That provision also exempts dividends distributed by an authorised collective investment scheme. It also exempts dividend or rental income received by a real estate investment company on behalf of its shareholders, where not less than 75% is distributed within 12 months after the end of the financial year in which it was earned.

The real estate investment company exemption does not exempt a shareholder from tax on the dividend or rental income received from the company. It does not exempt the company from tax on management fee, profits or other income earned on its own account. It does not exempt the company from tax on dividend or rental income if the stated conditions are not met.

<question>
My accountant still relies on section 23 of the Companies Income Tax Act for our exemptions. Does that section still apply to my company?
</question>
<gaps>

Whether the exemptions the company relies on are covered by section 163 of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 depends on facts about the company that are not in the question.

cases.rendered:
Notes
- The Companies Income Tax Act is not in the corpus this tool covers. Section numbers in the answer refer to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 or the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025.

From the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the Companies Income Tax Act, Cap. C21, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004 is repealed. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 196]

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 has its own income tax exemption provision. It exempts from tax under chapter two the profits or gains of listed persons, such as certain friendly societies, co-operative societies, bodies engaged in educational, religious or charitable activities of a public character, and registered trade unions, where the profits or gains are not derived from a trade or business carried on by them. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 163(1)(a) to (c)]

That provision also exempts dividends distributed by an authorised collective investment scheme. It also exempts dividend or rental income received by a real estate investment company on behalf of its shareholders, where not less than 75% is distributed within 12 months after the end of the financial year in which it was earned. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 163(1)(a) to (c)]

The real estate investment company exemption does not exempt a shareholder from tax on the dividend or rental income received from the company. It does not exempt the company from tax on management fee, profits or other income earned on its own account. It does not exempt the company from tax on dividend or rental income if the stated conditions are not met. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 163(1)(a) to (c)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not set out the text of section 23 of the Companies Income Tax Act, so they do not show which exemptions it covered.
- The passages do not contain any transitional or savings provision that might keep a repealed provision in effect for some purposes.
- The passages do not state the commencement date of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025.
- Whether the exemptions the company relies on are covered by section 163 of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 depends on facts about the company that are not in the question.

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 196 (gazette pages A 498, A 499)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 163(1)(a) to (c) (gazette pages A 476, A 477)

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 196: The gazette also repeals the Taxes and Levies (Approved List for Collection) Act; the National Assembly text does not. (DR-104)

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s3(1): the Nigeria Revenue Service has exclusive responsibility for taxes on companies and for value added tax; near miss for the state scope pattern.
cases.question: My state revenue office says I should pay my company's income tax to them. Which body actually handles company income tax and VAT?

claims.text: The Nigeria Revenue Service ("the Service") has exclusive responsibility to administer taxes on companies.
The Service's exclusive responsibility also covers taxes as contained in the Act, including value added tax and exemptions from value added tax.
The Service also has power to administer income tax, stamp duties and tax incentives.
Every company must file a self-assessment return with the Service at least once a year, whether or not it is liable to pay tax, with or without notice from the Service.
The Act defines "company" as a company or corporation, including a limited liability partnership, established by or under any law in force in Nigeria or elsewhere.

gaps: The passages do not say whether a state revenue office has any power to collect company income tax.
The passages do not say whether the questioner's business is a company within the definition, or whether any other provision changes who administers a particular tax.
The passages do not say where or to whom the tax is paid; they cover who administers the tax and who receives the returns.

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A company with an effective tax rate below 15% must recompute and pay additional tax to bring the rate to 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the company's furniture business counts as providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
- Whether the company's turnover and fixed assets are the gross turnover and total fixed assets the small company definition refers to is not stated, nor is whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group.
- Whether the company's tax rate for the year is 0% or 30% depends on those facts, which the passages do not settle.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as the ruling does not amount to an amendment or replacement of the law.

The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling when a taxable person applies. It must do so within 21 days of receiving the application, or give reasons in writing for being unable to issue the ruling.
The relevant tax authority means the Nigeria Revenue Service, or the Internal Revenue Service of a State or of the Federal Capital Territory in Nigeria.

An advance ruling includes a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, a proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification.
An application must be made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to a tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more such parties.

An application must contain the taxpayer's name, Tax ID, postal address, email address and telephone number. It must also contain a complete description of the issue or transaction and its financial implications, if any, and a complete description of the impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person. It must further give details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and earlier decisions of the authority on the issue, the statutory provisions or legal basis relied on, and the reasons the ruling should be granted. Finally, it must include a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.

The relevant tax authority may ask the applicant for more information. Where necessary, it shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications. The applicant may withdraw the application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The relevant tax authority may reject an application that requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, on an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, or on the interpretation of the Constitution. It may also reject one on an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or on a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or persons connected to the applicant.
A ruling is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given. It is based on the set of facts before the authority and cannot be of general application.

A ruling is void if the transaction actually carried out is materially different from the one described, if there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or if an assumption or condition set by the authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

A ruling ceases to be effective if the tax law provision it concerned is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it. It also ceases to be effective if a court overturns or modifies the interpretation of the tax law on which it is based, unless that decision is overturned.

The term company includes a company as defined under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, a corporate body formed under any other written law, and any association, whether incorporated in or outside Nigeria.

gaps: The passages do not say that a company is a taxable person or a party to a tax related issue for the purpose of applying for a ruling, so that link is not stated.
The prescribed form and manner for an application is not set out in the passages.

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s31 subsections (3) and (4): books must be in English, and records kept in another language need a certified English translation on demand; near miss for the other-country pattern.
cases.question: Our bookkeeper keeps the company's accounts in French. Is that allowed?

claims.text: Every person, including a company granted exemption from incorporation, shall maintain books or records of accounts, whether or not the person is liable to pay tax.
The books and records required to be maintained shall be in English language and, for the purpose of tax, shall be consistent with the format that may be prescribed by the relevant tax authority.

Where a record is maintained in a language other than the English language, the person shall, on demand by the tax authority, produce at its own expense a translation in English language, certified by a sworn translator.

A taxable person who fails to keep accounts, books and records of business transactions and income, to allow for the correct ascertainment of tax and filing of returns, is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the case of a company.
A taxable person who, upon request by the relevant tax authority, fails to provide any record or book prescribed in the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the case of a company.

"Book" includes any register, document or other records of information and any account or accounting record, however compiled, recorded or stored, including in written, printed, micro-film, digital, magnetic or electronic form.

gaps: The passages do not say whether keeping the books in French, with an English translation produced on demand, counts as meeting the English language requirement or avoids the penalty.
The passages do not say what format the relevant tax authority has prescribed.

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)

A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs and ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

If the Service grants an extension of the period for filing VAT returns, the extension does not extend the time to pay the tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The filing requirement in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

1 statement was removed because the cited provisions did not support it.

cases.rationale: Shares are chargeable assets (nta2025:s34); the share exemption needs proceeds under ₦150,000,000 and a gain not over ₦10,000,000, so it does not cover this gain, but reinvestment relief (proviso (iii)) may, and is a material proviso (D-43(b)). Gain = proceeds less cost (nta2025:s39 paragraph (b)), included in total profits (nta2025:s27(1)-(4)), rate nta2025:s56.
cases.question: Our company sold shares in another Nigerian company for ₦60 million; we paid ₦25 million for them. What tax do we owe on that gain?

claims.text: All forms of property, including shares, are chargeable assets for the purposes of this Part, whether situated in Nigeria or not, subject to exemptions in Part I of Chapter Eight of the Act.

Gains accruing to a person on disposal of shares in any Nigerian company shall not be chargeable gains where the disposal proceeds, in aggregate, are less than ₦150,000,000 and the chargeable gain does not exceed ₦10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months.

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company also shall not be chargeable gains where the shares are transferred between an approved borrower and a lender in a regulated securities lending transaction.

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company also shall not be chargeable gains where the proceeds are reinvested within the same year of assessment in acquiring shares in the same or other Nigerian companies, but tax shall accrue proportionately on the portion of the proceeds not reinvested in that manner.

A Nigerian company means a company formed, registered or incorporated under any law in Nigeria, or whose central place of management or control is Nigeria, or whose effective place of management or control is Nigeria.

gaps: The passages give no rate of tax on a chargeable gain, so the tax owed cannot be stated.
Working out the gain from the sale and purchase figures, and whether it exceeds the gain threshold in any 12 consecutive months, is a calculation the passages do not do.
The passages do not say whether the company made other disposals within 12 consecutive months, or whether the proceeds were reinvested in Nigerian company shares in the same year of assessment.
Part I of Chapter Eight, which section 34 refers to for exemptions, is not among the passages.
The passages do not say how a company's chargeable gains are brought into its taxable profits or how the tax is assessed on them.

cases.rendered:
All forms of property, including shares, are chargeable assets for the purposes of this Part, whether situated in Nigeria or not, subject to exemptions in Part I of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 34]

Gains accruing to a person on disposal of shares in any Nigerian company shall not be chargeable gains where the disposal proceeds, in aggregate, are less than ₦150,000,000 and the chargeable gain does not exceed ₦10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 34]

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company also shall not be chargeable gains where the shares are transferred between an approved borrower and a lender in a regulated securities lending transaction. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 34]

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company also shall not be chargeable gains where the proceeds are reinvested within the same year of assessment in acquiring shares in the same or other Nigerian companies, but tax shall accrue proportionately on the portion of the proceeds not reinvested in that manner. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 34]

A Nigerian company means a company formed, registered or incorporated under any law in Nigeria, or whose central place of management or control is Nigeria, or whose effective place of management or control is Nigeria. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "Nigerian company"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages give no rate of tax on a chargeable gain, so the tax owed cannot be stated.
- Working out the gain from the sale and purchase figures, and whether it exceeds the gain threshold in any 12 consecutive months, is a calculation the passages do not do.
- The passages do not say whether the company made other disposals within 12 consecutive months, or whether the proceeds were reinvested in Nigerian company shares in the same year of assessment.
- Part I of Chapter Eight, which section 34 refers to for exemptions, is not among the passages.
- The passages do not say how a company's chargeable gains are brought into its taxable profits or how the tax is assessed on them.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 34 (gazette page A 416)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "Nigerian company" (gazette page A 506)

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s30: a person who enters or intends to enter a transaction whose principal purpose is a tax advantage must give the information without notice or request (subsection (1)); timing and penalties are left to regulations (subsection (2)). Related: ntaa2025:s47 (counteracting avoidance).
cases.question: A consultant is offering us a scheme to cut our company tax bill. Do we have to tell the tax office about it?

claims.text: A person who enters or intends to enter into a transaction or agreement whose principal purpose is a benefit that enables, or might be expected to enable, that person to obtain a tax advantage shall, without notice or request, give the relevant tax authority information about it.

A tax advantage includes a relief or increased relief from tax, repayment or increased repayment of tax, avoidance or reduction of a charge to tax or an assessment to tax, avoidance of a possible assessment to tax, deferral of a payment of tax or advancement of a repayment of tax, or avoidance of an obligation to deduct or account for tax.
A transaction includes a course of action, agreement, scheme or arrangement.

The relevant tax authority may make regulations on the information to be provided, the form and manner of delivery, the period of time within which it shall be provided, and administrative penalties for non-disclosure, false disclosure, incomplete disclosure or late disclosure.

The relevant tax authority may counteract a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement by adjustments, disregarding or re-characterising it, in part or whole, unless the taxable person proves to the authority's satisfaction that granting the benefit would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Act or any other tax law.

A prohibited tax avoidance arrangement is one where, having regard to the facts and circumstances, it is reasonable to conclude that its main purpose was to obtain a tax benefit or advantage, that obtaining the advantage is contrary to the object and purpose of the tax provisions, that it results directly or indirectly in misuse or abuse of those provisions, or that it lacks commercial substance or coherence in whole or in part.

gaps: Whether the consultant's scheme has a principal purpose of obtaining a tax advantage depends on the scheme's facts, which are not given.
Any regulations made under section 30(2), including the time limit and penalties, are not among the passages.
Whether the scheme is a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement cannot be decided without the scheme's details.

cases.rationale: nta2025:s202:def:small-company: turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less and fixed assets not over ₦250,000,000, professional services excluded, so ₦65 million turnover fails the test; the rate is then 30% (nta2025:s56).
cases.question: Our catering company's turnover grew to ₦65 million this year, but our fixed assets are only ₦20 million. Are we still a small company for income tax?

claims.text: A small company is defined as a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000.
Any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.
Under the tax rates section, a small company is taxed at 0% on its total profits, and any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants.

The Tax Administration Act has a separate definition of "small business" with a gross turnover limit of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum and total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, again excluding any business providing professional services.

gaps: Whether the company's turnover figure counts as gross turnover as defined is not stated in the passages.
Whether a catering company counts as a business providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
Comparing the company's figures with the limits is a calculation or comparison left to the reader and is not done here.
Which definition applies to the company's income tax position beyond the Nigeria Tax Act definition of small company is not stated in the passages.

cases.rendered:
A small company is defined as a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under the tax rates section, a small company is taxed at 0% on its total profits, and any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover"]

The Tax Administration Act has a separate definition of "small business" with a gross turnover limit of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum and total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, again excluding any business providing professional services. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the company's turnover figure counts as gross turnover as defined is not stated in the passages.
- Whether a catering company counts as a business providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
- Comparing the company's figures with the limits is a calculation or comparison left to the reader and is not done here.
- Which definition applies to the company's income tax position beyond the Nigeria Tax Act definition of small company is not stated in the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover" (gazette pages A 504, A 505)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)

cases.rationale: An insurance sum for damage or loss of assets is a disposal (nta2025:s35 subsection (2)(b)). nta2025:s43: if applied within three years to a replacement, a chargeable gain arises when compensation plus scrap value exceeds the replacement cost; otherwise an additional asset for capital allowance. cases.question: Our warehouse burnt down and the insurer paid us. If we use the money to build a replacement, is any of the payout taxed?

claims.text: Where an asset is lost or destroyed, and a capital sum received as compensation for the loss or destruction is applied within three years of receipt in acquiring another asset in its replacement, the owner is deemed to make a chargeable gain if the compensation received together with the residual or scrap value is greater than the cost of the replacement asset.

If the compensation together with the residual or scrap value is lower than the cost of the replacement asset, the owner is deemed, for the purposes of the First Schedule, to have acquired an additional asset for an amount equal to the cost of the new asset less the compensation together with the residual or scrap value.
Except for that additional asset, allowance claimed on the new asset for the purposes of the First Schedule is limited to the residue of the old asset, if any.
The definition of building includes a warehouse, and means a structure permanently affixed to land for all or most of its useful life.

The rights under a policy of insurance other than those under a capital redemption business or industrial assurance business do not constitute an asset on the disposal of which a chargeable gain may accrue, except as expressly provided under Part VIII.

The passages do not say whether a replacement that is built, rather than bought, counts as acquiring another asset.
The passages do not say what kind of insurance policy the business holds.

claims.text: The Service may direct a taxable person to whom a taxable supply is made in Nigeria, and who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service.

Remission of VAT under section 155(1) and (2) is to be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six must keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person.
A taxable person is to pay VAT to a supplier on the taxable supply made to the person, and the VAT so paid is known as input VAT.
Section 155 is expressed to be without prejudice to any provision of this Act or any other tax law.

cases.rendered:
The Service may direct a taxable person to whom a taxable supply is made in Nigeria, and who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

Remission of VAT under section 155(1) and (2) is to be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six must keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

A taxable person is to pay VAT to a supplier on the taxable supply made to the person, and the VAT so paid is known as input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152]

Section 155 is expressed to be without prejudice to any provision of this Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

cases.question: Our supplier refunded part of a cost we had already deducted. What does section 193 say happens to that refund?

claims.text: Where a deduction has been allowed under the Act for a liability or an expense incurred, and the expense is refunded in whole or in part, the amount refunded is income on the day of the refund.

Where a liability or expenditure of a capital nature is waived, it is a chargeable gain for the purposes of Part VIII of Chapter Two of the Act.
Section 20(3) says that a liability waived, released or recovered is included in the assessable profits or chargeable gains in accordance with section 193.

must_not: claim that the bakery must file monthly VAT returns with no mention of the small-business exemption
cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s22(1)-(10): monthly returns by the 21st (subsection (1)) do not apply to a small business (subsection (4)), which may opt in (5). ntaa2025:s147:def:small-business: turnover ₦100,000,000 or less and fixed assets under ₦250,000,000, professional services excluded; the bakery qualifies on the stated figures.
cases.question: We run a bakery with yearly sales of about ₦80 million and equipment worth ₦30 million. Must we file VAT returns every month?

claims.text: A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month, with or without a notice, and whether or not an economic activity has taken place.
The monthly filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business.

A small business means a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business.

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. This does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations as defined in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025.
A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns.

In deciding whether a person meets the small company threshold, the value of supplies of the person's capital assets is excluded, as is the value of supplies made solely as a consequence of selling the whole or part of the business or permanently ceasing to carry on business.

gaps: Whether the bakery's sales and equipment figures fit the small business definition depends on facts not in the passages, such as whether the ₦80 million is gross turnover and whether the ₦30 million is total fixed assets.
The passages do not say whether a bakery is a business providing professional services.
Whether the bakery has opted out of the small business exemption is not stated.

<question>
We run a bakery with yearly sales of about ₦80 million and equipment worth ₦30 million. Must we file VAT returns every month?
</question>
<gaps>
<gap index="0">
Whether the bakery has opted out of the small business exemption is not stated.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month, with or without a notice, and whether or not an economic activity has taken place. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The monthly filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A small business means a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. This does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations as defined in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

In deciding whether a person meets the small company threshold, the value of supplies of the person's capital assets is excluded, as is the value of supplies made solely as a consequence of selling the whole or part of the business or permanently ceasing to carry on business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the bakery's sales and equipment figures fit the small business definition depends on facts not in the passages, such as whether the ₦80 million is gross turnover and whether the ₦30 million is total fixed assets.
- The passages do not say whether a bakery is a business providing professional services.
- Whether the bakery has opted out of the small business exemption is not stated.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10) (gazette page A 277)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)

- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-references: subsection (4), sections 105 and 107 (cited) against subsection (5), sections 100 and 102 (National Assembly). (DR-198)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-reference: section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act (cited) against section 151 (National Assembly text, the same section under its numbering, DR-000). (DR-199)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)

claims.text: A taxable person who disputes a tax assessment may apply to the relevant tax authority for revision and amendment of the assessment, by a written notice of objection delivered in person, by courier service or via electronic means.

An objection application is valid only if it is delivered to the relevant tax authority within 30 days from the date of service of the disputed notice of assessment and it contains the grounds of objection set out in section 41(2)(b).

Despite the 30-day period, the relevant tax authority may, for any satisfactory and good cause shown, extend the time for making the application to such reasonable time in the particular circumstances.
The relevant tax authority shall respond to the objection notice within 90 days, otherwise the objection of the taxpayer shall be upheld.

Where no valid objection or appeal has been lodged within the time stipulated under the Act, the assessment is final and conclusive for all purposes of the Act as regards the amount of the total income or profits assessed.

A taxable person who disputes a tax assessment may apply to the relevant tax authority for revision and amendment of the assessment, by a written notice of objection delivered in person, by courier service or via electronic means. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(1) to (4)]

An objection application is valid only if it is delivered to the relevant tax authority within 30 days from the date of service of the disputed notice of assessment and it contains the grounds of objection set out in section 41(2)(b). [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(1) to (4)]

Despite the 30-day period, the relevant tax authority may, for any satisfactory and good cause shown, extend the time for making the application to such reasonable time in the particular circumstances. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(1) to (4)]

The relevant tax authority shall respond to the objection notice within 90 days, otherwise the objection of the taxpayer shall be upheld. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(5) to (8)]

Where no valid objection or appeal has been lodged within the time stipulated under the Act, the assessment is final and conclusive for all purposes of the Act as regards the amount of the total income or profits assessed. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 43]

<question>
Our company paid ₦7.5 million of income tax two months after it fell due. Tell me the exact naira penalty and interest we now owe.
</question>
<gaps>
<gap index="0">
The passages do not say whether the 10% sum applies to the full amount paid late, or whether the tax was paid within any extension.
</gap>
</gaps>

cases.rendered:
Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of the tax payable is added to it. This is subject to section 67, which is not among the passages. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

For naira remittances, unpaid tax carries interest at the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread to be determined by the Minister, from the date the tax becomes payable until it is paid. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

For foreign currency remittances, unpaid tax incurs interest at the prevailing Secured Overnight Financing Rate or any successor rate, plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines, from the date the tax becomes payable until it is paid. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The interest under section 65(1)(b) and (c) is compound interest. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The penalty and interest are not treated as part of the tax paid for the purpose of claiming relief under the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Any balance of tax unpaid at the due date attracts interest and penalties as provided in the Act or any other relevant law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Where the tax authority grants an extension for payment and the person fails to pay within the extension, penalty and interest accrue from the original due date as if no extension was granted. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

The relevant tax authority may, for good cause shown, remit the whole or any part of penalty or interest due under the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 66]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The exact naira figure needs a calculation of 10% of the tax and of compound interest, which is not done here.
- The Central Bank of Nigeria monetary policy rate and the Minister's spread are not among the passages, so the interest rate cannot be stated.
- Whether the tax was paid in naira or foreign currency is not stated in the question.
- Section 67, to which section 65(1) is made subject, is not among the passages.
- The passages do not say whether the 10% sum applies to the full amount paid late, or whether the tax was paid within any extension.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65 (gazette pages A 298, A 299)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6) (gazette pages A 288, A 289)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 66 (gazette page A 299)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Interest is SOFR plus 10% or such other spread as the authority determines in the cited text; the National Assembly text says SOFR plus a spread to be determined, without the 10%. (DR-243)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Only the cited text makes the interest in subsection (1)(b) and (c) compound and applies it to tax debts unpaid at commencement. (DR-245)

claims.text: Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

Where a person appointed under subsection (3) has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the person appointed has failed to collect the VAT.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 shall be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

A person having an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six of the Act shall keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person.

cases.rendered:
Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 151]

A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 151]

The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 151]

Where a person appointed under subsection (3) has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the person appointed has failed to collect the VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 151]

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 shall be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

The remission must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

A person having an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six of the Act shall keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

- The passages do not say whether the vendor's cloud software is a taxable supply.
- The passages do not say whether the vendor has been appointed by the Service to collect VAT, or whether it has failed to collect it.

- The passages do not say whether the business is a taxable person.
- Whether a supply from Dublin counts as made from outside Nigeria is not stated in the passages.

Sources

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155 (gazette page A 474)

Company tax for each year of assessment is levied on the total profits of every company at 0% for a small company and at 30 per cent for any other company from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A development levy of 4% on assessable profits applies to companies chargeable to tax under Chapters Two and Three, other than small companies and non-resident companies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 59]

The minimum effective tax rate rule (top-up to 15%) applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the business's turnover and fixed assets are measured as the question describes (for example, whether the machines and premises are the company's total fixed assets) is not stated in the passages, and the comparison of the stated figures with the thresholds is left to the reader.
- Whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group is not stated in the question.
- Whether making and selling fruit juice counts as providing professional services is not covered by the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 59 (gazette page A 427)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.question: The NRS served us an assessment we believe is wrong. How long do we have to object, and what must our objection contain?

claims.text: A taxable person who disputes a tax assessment may apply to the relevant tax authority, by written notice of objection delivered in person, by courier service or via electronic means, for the revision and amendment of the assessment.

An objection application is only valid if it is delivered to the relevant tax authority within 30 days from the date of service of the disputed notice of assessment, and it contains the grounds of objection.
The grounds must also state the amendment required to resolve the dispute or correct the error, and the justification for the amendments.
The grounds must also state the amount of assessable and total profits, income or value of transactions admitted by the taxable person for the relevant reporting period.
The grounds must also state the amount of tax admitted by the taxable person, or that no amount of tax is admitted as payable.

Despite the 30-day period, the relevant tax authority may, for any satisfactory and good cause shown, extend the time for making the application to such reasonable time in the particular circumstances.

After receiving the notice of objection, the relevant tax authority may require the taxable person to furnish particulars it deems necessary and to produce all books or other documents relating to the profits, income or transactions of the taxable person.
The relevant tax authority shall respond to the objection notice within 90 days, otherwise the objection of the taxpayer shall be upheld.
Where the authority considers the notice of objection invalid, or the parties do not agree on the amount of tax to be assessed, the taxpayer may exercise the right of appeal.
An assessment becomes final and conclusive as to the amount of total income or profits where no valid objection or appeal has been lodged within the time stipulated under the Act.
